question.problem: Consider the function $f:{R}^{3}\to R$ defined by $f(x)={x}_{1}{x}_{2}+3{x}_{1}{x}_{3}+{x}_{2}{x}_{3}.$ What is the total derivative of $f$ with respect to $x$ at ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]?$
question.worked_solution:
The total derivative of a scalar-valued function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ with respect to a vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ is the row vector

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{1\times n}.
$$

In our case, the function 

- acts on a vector $x\in {R}^{3},$ and

- outputs a scalar $f(x)\in R$ defined by 

$$
f(x)={x}_{1}{x}_{2}+3{x}_{1}{x}_{3}+{x}_{2}{x}_{3}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{2}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{3}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}{x}_{2}+3{x}_{1}{x}_{3}+{x}_{2}{x}_{3}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}{x}_{2}+3{x}_{1}{x}_{3}+{x}_{2}{x}_{3}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{3}}({x}_{1}{x}_{2}+3{x}_{1}{x}_{3}+{x}_{2}{x}_{3})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} & {x}_{1}+{x}_{3} & 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{1\times 3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the total derivative at ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}({x}_{0}) & =[\begin{aligned}0+3(2) & 1+2 & 3(1)+0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 & 3 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
